series.name: Flora de la República de Cuba
series.when: Cuba; only some family fascicles digitized

bibdigital.notes: Host for scanned floras. Works are flora_iberica and flora_slovenska. Browse the Flora category only when no registered work treated the species. Cite idurl/1/{id}. Skip pamphlets, exsiccata, red lists, and fungi.

series.name: Flora Polska jawnokwiatowych rodzajów (Waga)
series.when: Kingdom of Poland; 1847–48 vascular flora (T. 1 on RCIN)

series.name: W. Szafer Institute of Botany — library collections
series.when: IB PAN library scans: floras, keys, monographs

series.name: W. Szafer Institute of Botany — own editions
series.when: Polish Botanical Studies, guidebooks, stand-alone monographs

series.name: W. Szafer Institute of Botany
series.when: Institute hub; mix of literature and collections

rcin.notes: Digital Repository of Scientific Institutes (Polish Academy of Sciences). Host for scanned Polish and Central European floras and Szafer Institute papers. Work is flora_polska. Search the Latin name; cite publication/{id}. Skip herbarium specimens (vascular plants / botanical collections), fungi, palaeobotany, and red lists.

ruj.notes: Jagiellonian University Repository (Repozytorium Uniwersytetu Jagiellońskiego). Host for Central European botanical papers (e.g. Mitka on Aconitum moldavicum in Fragmenta Floristica et Geobotanica Polonica / Roczniki Bieszczadzkie). Work is ruj. Search the Latin name; open a paper that actually treats that plant and cite handle/item/{id}. Skip theses or records that only mention the name, non-vascular papers, and items with no downloadable text.

sources.name: English Wikipedia
sources.notes: First-class pipeline source via the Wikipedia API. Skip culture, culinary, and toxicity-in-pets sections.

sources.name: World Checklist of Vascular Plants
sources.notes: Local sqlite only. Live POWO is Cloudflare-blocked; do not scrape POWO.

sources.name: Plants For A Future
sources.notes: Reliable habitat line, flowering/seed months, and 'ornamental' / woodland-garden notes. Ignore the related-plants table.

sources.name: Useful Temperate Plants
sources.notes: PFAF sister. Same Ken Fern data; check if PFAF is thin. Do not auto-fetch both.

sources.name: Royal Horticultural Society
sources.notes: Garden measurements (flower length, raceme count, height) and planting types. Search first; plant IDs are not Latin names. Award of Garden Merit supports filterHabitat 2.

sources.name: Alpine Garden Society Plant Encyclopaedia
sources.notes: Short English alpine-plant treatments (leaves, scape, flower, a habitat line). URL /plants/{Genus}/{epithet}. Horticultural encyclopaedia, not a flora; does not by itself support filterHabitat 2. 404 is normal outside the encyclopaedia.

sources.name: Lilium Species Foundation
sources.notes: Best wild-habitat and morphology notes for Lilium. Grassland/scrub ecotones, rocky slopes, winter rosette.

sources.name: Go Botany (Native Plant Trust)
sources.notes: New England / northeast North America. Useful when a species is naturalized there. 404 is normal for plants absent from the region.

sources.name: Minnesota Wildflowers
sources.notes: Structured English for Minnesota / north-central USA: habit, height, flowering months, flower, leaf, stem, fruit, habitat. Search the Latin name; 404 or a miss is normal outside that flora. Skip lookalikes so another species is not copied.

sources.name: SEINet (Southwest US herbaria portal)
sources.notes: Symbiota taxon page for south-western / central US species. Usable only when the page carries a description block (Morton Arboretum vPlants for the Chicago region, SW Field Guide for AZ/NM, sometimes FNA). Metric measurements, flowering months, elevation, habitat. A page with only specimens and images = no treatment; skip. Skip the Similar species paragraph so another species is not copied.

sources.name: Kansas Wildflowers & Grasses
sources.notes: Mike Haddock's Kansas flora. Structured English: stem, leaves, inflorescence, flower, fruit, habitat, height and flowering months, in inches. 404 is normal outside Kansas. Skip the Uses and Comments sections for the seven fields.

sources.name: Native Plants of South Dakota (SDSU Open PRAIRIE)
sources.notes: R. Neil Reese's Native Plants of South Dakota records: one metric paragraph (habit, stem length, leaf, inflorescence, calyx, corolla, fruit) plus South Dakota flowering months and habitat. Record ids are numeric, so web-search the Latin name to find the page. Skip the Horticulture Notes for the seven fields.

sources.name: Digital Atlas of the Virginia Flora
sources.notes: Virginia Botanical Associates / Flora of Virginia project. One habitat line, Virginia frequency by region, native status and common names; no morphology. Search is JS-only: browse index.php?do=browse:group&id=4 (Dicots) -> family -> species, plant ids are numeric (e.g. Ruellia caroliniensis = index.php?do=plant&plant=772). No entry is normal outside Virginia.

sources.name: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox
sources.notes: North Carolina State University extension profiles: short description, height/width in feet, bloom months, flower/leaf/stem/fruit attribute lines, a one-line habitat, common names. Horticultural and imperial, so a flora should carry the measurements; the Landscape and Wildlife Value sections do not by themselves support filterHabitat 2. URL slug is lower-case genus-epithet. 404 is normal outside the south-eastern USA.

sources.name: Vascular Plants of Williamson County (UT Austin)
sources.notes: A. C. Gibson's very detailed metric treatments (stems, leaves, inflorescence, flower, fruit) for central Texas. URL uses a %20-separated Latin name. 404 is normal outside Williamson County. No habitat or flowering data.

sources.name: Illinois Wildflowers
sources.notes: John Hilty's Illinois / Midwest flora. Long English description (height, leaves, umbel, flower, fruit, root), blooming period and a habitat list, in inches. Page slugs are common-name based (e.g. prairie/plantx/vlt_sorrelx.htm), so search the Latin name; 404 is normal outside Illinois. Skip the Faunal Associations and Cultivation sections and lookalikes so another species is not copied.

sources.name: Pacific Bulb Society wiki
sources.notes: Bulb genera. Page titles are irregular (section pages, not always the binomial).

sources.name: Flora of Israel Online
sources.notes: Good for Balkans / Turkey / Levant plants (e.g. Lilium candidum). URLs use a short code, not the Latin name.

sources.name: Flora of Greece
sources.notes: Hellenic Botanical Society / BGBM treatments. Species pages are UUID URLs on portal.cybertaxonomy.org, not Latin slugs; genus PDFs live under https://media.e-taxonomy.eu/flora-greece/pdf/. 404 is normal outside Greece and the Aegean.

sources.name: Minnesota DNR invasive plants
sources.notes: Concrete habitat lists (grassland, prairie, forest edge, yards) for species invasive in the US Midwest. Do not treat noxious-weed status as habitat text.

sources.name: Missouri Plants
sources.notes: Excellent structured English: habit, stems, leaves, inflorescence, flowers, fruits, flowering months, habitat. Missouri / central US flora; 404 is normal for plants not in that flora. Skip lookalikes so another species is not copied.

sources.name: NatureGate / Luontoportti
sources.notes: Reliable morphological English: growing form, height, flower, leaf, fruit, habitat. Nordic/Finnish flora — no page is normal (e.g. Digitalis lanata, Lilium candidum). Search scientific name only; ignore article mentions of other species.

sources.name: EPPO Global Database
sources.notes: Best multilingual common-name table. Search the preferred scientific name, then use https://gd.eppo.int/taxon/{EPPO-code}. Take only names printed for that language. A miss or an empty table is normal. Do not use a hybrid/group hit (e.g. Lilium candidum hybrids).

sources.name: BOTANY.cz
sources.notes: Reliable Central European flora. Czech pages have Popis, Ekologie, Rozšíření, and Czech/Slovak names; some species also have English. Latin slug /cs/{genus-epithet}/; try /en/ first. 404 is normal. Skip related-article and prev/next links so another species is not copied.

sources.name: Pladias (Czech flora and vegetation)
sources.notes: Czech flora trait database (Kaplan et al. height and flowering months; habitat optima; forest affinity). Latin URL /en/taxon/data/{Genus%20epithet}. Reliable for native Czech species. Skip Ellenberg numbers in user-facing English.

sources.name: Flóra Slovenska

volumes.covers: Cistales, Begoniales, Tamaricales, Elatinales, Violales, Cucurbitales, Campanulales
Mycota, Erysiphales (powdery mildews) — not vascular plants

sources.notes: Slovak Academy of Sciences national flora (Futák, Bertová, Goliašová et al.; VEDA, Bratislava). Slovak morphological treatments and Slovak vernaculars. Cite https://bibdigital.rjb.csic.es/idurl/1/{id} for the volume that actually treats the species; do not invent a page. Viewer/OCR is often behind a captcha — if the box has no text, skip that volume. Not in this library: VI/2 (Asteraceae, 2024–). X/1–X/2 are fungi. Series hub: https://bibdigital.rjb.csic.es/records/item/15084-flora-slovenska. Skip if the plant is absent from the Slovak flora.

sources.name: Flora Polska
sources.notes: Polish vascular flora of Poland and adjacent lands (Szafer / Pawłowski, 1919–1980, 14 vols.; Waga 1847 on RCIN as publication 3349). Polish text. Search the Latin name on RCIN dLibra and open a page that actually treats that plant. Do not mark reliable until a volume is used. Skip herbarium specimens, fungi, and spore-plant volumes. Polish vernaculars are for pl names only — never as English labels.

sources.name: Jagiellonian University Repository
sources.notes: Reliable Central European botanical papers (Poland, Carpathians, adjacent lands). Search the Latin name and use a paper that actually treats that species (example: Aconitum moldavicum). English or Polish. Polish vernaculars are for pl names only — never as English labels. 404 / empty search is normal when nothing treats the plant.

sources.name: Flora Iberica

volumes.covers: Platanaceae–Plumbaginaceae (part); includes Caryophyllaceae, Portulacaceae, Polygonaceae, Amaranthaceae, Chenopodiaceae

sources.notes: Modern vascular flora of the Iberian Peninsula and Balearic Islands (Castroviejo et al., RJB-CSIC). Spanish keys and descriptions. Cite the volume that treats the family. Official PDFs also at http://www.floraiberica.es/ — prefer a page that actually covers this plant. Skip if the species is absent from Iberia/Balearics.

sources.name: eFloras (FOC, FNA and others)
sources.notes: Already used in the live catalog. Flora of China and Flora of North America treatments.

sources.name: Burke Herbarium Image Collection
sources.notes: Washington / Pacific Northwest flora. Habitat, flowering months, and a concise morphological treatment; often embeds the FNA description. URL uses a space-separated Latin name. 404 is normal for plants absent from that flora.

sources.name: E-Flora BC
sources.notes: Electronic Atlas of the Flora of British Columbia. Often embeds The Illustrated Flora of British Columbia: habit, height, leaves, heads, corolla, fruit, and a short habitat line. Useful for Eurasian species naturalized in western Canada. 404 or an empty description is normal outside that flora.

sources.name: Jepson eFlora
sources.notes: California flora. Concise English treatment: habit, stem, leaf, inflorescence, flower, fruit, ecology, flowering months. Useful for Eurasian species naturalized in California. 404 is normal outside that flora.

sources.name: Flora of New Zealand
sources.notes: Landcare Research treatments of native and naturalised vascular plants. Latin URL /factsheet/Taxon/{Genus}-{epithet}.html. Useful for European species naturalised in New Zealand. 404 is normal outside that flora. Southern-hemisphere flowering months stay in the changelog, not as catalog months.

sources.name: Ontario Rock Garden & Hardy Plant Society
sources.notes: Occasional habitat one-liners (grassland, woodland edge). Pages can be thin or empty.

sources.name: BSBI / Plant Atlas 2020
sources.notes: British and Irish flora. Search the Latin name on bsbi.org; Plant Atlas 2020 has habitat, status and biogeography. No page is normal outside Britain and Ireland. Do not copy Vice-County lists into user English.

sources.name: JN Ecology (Brambles of the British Isles)
sources.notes: John Norton British and Irish Rubus microspecies accounts. Morphology (flowers, stamens, leaves, stems) and a short habitat line. Latin slug /rubus/accounts/{epithet}.htm. No page is normal outside that treatment. Skip lookalikes so another bramble is not copied.

sources.name: Info Flora (Switzerland)
sources.notes: Swiss flora. Species pages often embed Flora Helvetica height, flowering months, head and fruit measurements. URLs use a vernacular slug, not the Latin name. Skip ecological indicator numbers in user-facing English.

sources.name: FloraWeb (BfN)
sources.notes: German BfN species factsheets. Galium pages often split s.str. from the aggregate (e.g. G. mollugo L. s.str.). Search the Latin name; IDs are not Latin. Skip Ellenberg numbers in user-facing English.

sources.name: Tela Botanica (eFlore / Coste)
sources.notes: French collaborative flora. Species pages are https://www.tela-botanica.org/bdtfx-nn-{num}, not Latin slugs; search the scientific name. Coste descriptions give height, flower size, flowering months and a habitat line. French vernaculars are for fr names only — never as English labels. No page is normal outside France.

sources.name: Flora-On
sources.notes: Portuguese Botanical Society atlas (continental Portugal, Azores, Madeira). Habitat/ecology line, life form, and phenology charts. Latin query ?q={Genus+epithet}. Portuguese vernaculars are for pt names only. No page is normal outside that flora.

sources.name: Acta Plantarum
sources.notes: Italian volunteer flora. Species pages are numeric IDs, not Latin slugs; search the scientific name. Italian text with a short morphological card (habit, fruit, leaves). Italian vernaculars are for it names only. No page is normal outside Italy. Skip forum lookalikes so another species is not copied.

sources.name: Bilder ur Nordens flora (Lindman)
sources.notes: Carl Lindman, Bilder ur Nordens flora (2nd ed., 1917–1926) on Project Runeberg. Plate pages, not Latin URLs. Search the Latin or Swedish name. Swedish text; use only when the plate treats this plant.

sources.name: Wiegleb, Ranunculus sect. Batrachium (Flora von Deutschland)
sources.notes: G. Wiegleb 2020 treatment of Ranunculus sect. Batrachium for Flora von Deutschland. PDF, not a Latin URL. Use only when that species is treated. German text. Skip lookalikes so another water-crowfoot is not copied.

sources.name: Flora of Zimbabwe
sources.notes: Hyde, Wursten, Ballings & Coates Palgrave, Flora of Zimbabwe (sister sites for Mozambique, Zambia, Malawi, Botswana). Species pages are speciesdata/species.php?species_id=N; find N from speciesdata/index.php → family.php → genus.php (the search form is POST-only). Description, habitat, flowering time (southern hemisphere: changelog only), worldwide distribution, common names with language tags. Some species are split into varieties (e.g. Nymphaea nouchali var. caerulea); say so in the changelog. Absence is normal outside the Flora Zambesiaca area.

sources.name: Flora of Australia (ALA profiles)
sources.notes: ABRS Flora of Australia treatments served by the Atlas of Living Australia profile hub. The HTML page is JavaScript-rendered; append /json to the profile URL and read profile.attributes (Description, Phenology, Distribution, Habitat, Common Name, Source). 'Not Found' is normal outside that flora. Southern-hemisphere flowering seasons stay in the changelog, not as catalog months.

sources.name: PlantNET (New South Wales Flora Online)
sources.notes: Royal Botanic Gardens Sydney, New South Wales Flora Online. Concise English treatment of native and naturalised species (habit, leaves, inflorescence, corolla, fruit, flowering, distribution, common name). Species URL uses Genus~epithet. A page that only lists the name as a synonym of another species is not a treatment. Southern-hemisphere flowering months stay in the changelog, not as catalog months.
